descriptor: Winding wires, conductors and power cables (BSE SME)
lede: A Rajasthan-based maker of aluminium and copper winding wires, conductors and power cables that doubled revenue in FY26 and listed on BSE SME in 2026, riding India's power-distribution spending. Margins have risen from 2% to 12% in three years, but the business burns cash, leans on promoter loans and a promoter-group trading firm, and its first earnings call left more questions than answers.

short_version.text: Revenue doubled to ₹269 Cr in FY26 and Q1 FY27 rose 279% to ₹95 Cr at a ~12% EBITDA margin; order book ₹142 Cr plus ₹150 Cr pipeline, and capacity rises 60% from February 2027 for only ₹15-20 Cr of capex.

Operating cash flow negative three years running (–₹10 Cr in FY26), debt/equity ~1.7x before the IPO, ₹17 Cr owed to small suppliers at year end, and purchases from a promoter-group firm jumped to ₹11 Cr. The edited call transcript contradicts itself on margins and product mix.
~24x trailing earnings and ~21x EV/EBITDA, against Ram Ratna Wires at 46x and Diamond Power at 111x; cheaper, but much smaller and less proven.

blocks.text: Susan Electricals makes aluminium and copper winding wires (used in transformers and motors), aluminium conductors, and LT, HT and MVCC power cables, selling to state utilities and DISCOMs, EPC contractors such as Montecarlo and RVNL, and private buyers. Orders are mostly tender-based, with supply starting 45-60 days after order.

items.text: Moving from winding wires to higher-value HT and MVCC cables, which management says can earn ~20% at product level.
Blended EBITDA margin ~12% in Q1 FY27, up from ~2% in FY23.
Aluminium price swings are handled through pricing, with little detail given.
Revenue from ₹55 Cr (FY22) to ₹269 Cr (FY26); PAT from ₹0.8 Cr (FY24) to ₹18 Cr.
Listed on BSE SME in 2026; IPO money for capacity and working capital.
Board reshuffled in late 2025: new whole-time directors, CFO and company secretary.

items.text: Promoters (Jain family) hold 67.0%; no pledge.
Domestic institutions 13.5%, foreign 2.1%; ~1,250 shareholders.
Purchases from promoter-group firm SMV Enterprises rose to ₹11.2 Cr (from ₹0.6 Cr), plus sales, rent and job work; AGM asked to approve these as material related-party transactions.
Funded by promoter loans: CMD lent ₹9.2 Cr and was repaid ₹9.6 Cr during FY26; ₹4 Cr still outstanding.
The 'transcript' is an edited summary with contradictory numbers; analysts asked for clearer disclosure.
Modest pay: CMD ₹19.5 lakh in FY26.

blocks.text: Large cable makers (Polycab, KEI, RR Kabel) dominate branded cables; Susan competes in utility tenders where price and approvals matter most.

blocks.text: Scenarios are illustrative, built on our assumptions, not company guidance.

Susan is growing fast in a strong market and is cheaper than listed cable peers, but it is a small, cash-hungry, newly listed company with related-party trading and patchy disclosure. Treat the growth as unproven until cash flow turns positive and a second call gives consistent numbers.
